findings.issue: HttpOnly cookie property is in the Servlet namespace and has no effect on Spring WebFlux. `server.servlet.session.cookie.http-only=true` is a Servlet stack property; the application uses Spring WebFlux (reactive). WebFlux session cookie properties live under `server.reactive.session.cookie.*`. As written, the HttpOnly flag is silently NOT applied to the SESSION cookie, exposing it to JavaScript and XSS-based session theft.
findings.suggestion:
Replace the property with the correct WebFlux namespace:
  server.reactive.session.cookie.http-only=true
  server.reactive.session.cookie.same-site=strict
  server.reactive.session.cookie.secure=true
Also add `secure=true` (HTTPS enforcement in production) and `same-site` here so all cookie security attributes are in one place.

findings.issue: Super-admin password falls back to an empty string. The property `app.super-admin.password=${SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD:}` has an empty default. If `SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD` is not set, the SuperAdminSeeder will create or update the super-admin account with a blank password — effectively an unauthenticated privileged account. There is no fail-fast guard at the configuration layer.

The example super-admin password `changeme123` is a weak, commonly known default. While `.env.example` is intentionally committed and not a real secret, publishing a concrete weak password as the example normalises it as an acceptable value and increases the probability that developers will use it verbatim in staging or CI environments.
findings.suggestion:
Replace with a clearly unusable placeholder that communicates minimum requirements:
  SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD=<min-12-chars-letters-digits-symbols>
This makes it obvious the value must be replaced and communicates the password policy without providing a usable default.

findings.issue: Mailpit container uses an unpinned `latest` image tag (`axllent/mailpit:latest`), while MongoDB and Redis use pinned tags (`mongo:8.0`, `redis:7.4`). Using `latest` means any `docker compose pull` can silently introduce a different (potentially breaking or compromised) image version, violating build reproducibility. This is a supply-chain hygiene issue for local dev.
findings.suggestion:
Pin to a specific digest or semver tag, consistent with the other services:
  image: axllent/mailpit:v1.21
Check the current latest release at https://github.com/axllent/mailpit/releases and pin to it.

summary: Four findings across three files. The most significant is the HttpOnly cookie misconfiguration (major): `server.servlet.session.cookie.http-only` has no effect on a WebFlux app — the correct namespace is `server.reactive.session.cookie.*` — meaning session cookies will lack the HttpOnly flag and be accessible to JavaScript. The second major finding is the empty-string fallback for `SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, which can produce a privileged account with no password if the env var is missing. Two minor findings: the `.env.example` weak password example and the unpinned `latest` Mailpit image. No hardcoded production secrets or critical vulnerabilities were found. The .gitignore correctly excludes `.env` and `.env.*` while committing only `.env.example`. All ports are correctly bound to 127.0.0.1. The JobRunr dashboard is correctly disabled. Dependency versions look appropriate.
